newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Congress members advocate separating tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Congress members advocate separating tax cuts.

text.p: A bipartisan group of members of the House of Representatives Thursday sent a letter to House Speaker Newt Gingrich supporting separating tax cuts from the budget process.
The group was led by Republican Reps. Mike Castle of Delaware and Fred Upton of Michigan and Democrat Reps. John Tanner of Tennessee and Charlie Stenholm of Texas.
The two Democrats are also members of the so-called "Blue Dog" Democrats who advocate against including tax cuts in putting together a balanced budget.

"We believe that considering tax cut legislation separately from the budget significantly improves the chances for an agreement to balance the federal budget by 2002," the letter signed by 56 members of the House said.
"While most of us believe that some form of tax relief should be considered this year, we wholeheartedly agree that a balanced budget agreement should come first," the letter said.
